questions.question: "Ischemic colitis" most commonly involves the "watershed" area of the splenic flexure, also known as:
questions.detail: Griffiths point is the critical watershed area where the territories of the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) and inferior mesenteric artery (IMA) meet.

questions.question: A "lead pipe" appearance of the colon (loss of haustration) is a classic feature of chronic:
questions.detail: Chronic inflammation in ulcerative colitis leads to a shortened, featureless, and non-haustrated colon.

questions.question: "Toxic megacolon" is a potentially fatal complication of ulcerative colitis characterized by:
choices: B. Massive colonic dilation (>6 cm) and systemic toxicity
questions.detail: Toxic megacolon is a surgical emergency due to the significant risk of colonic perforation.

questions.question: Pseudomembranous colitis is an inflammatory condition of the colon almost always caused by:
questions.detail: This condition results from an antibiotic-related overgrowth of toxin-producing C. difficile bacteria.

questions.question: Which of the following is a classic imaging sign of "appendicitis" on CT?
questions.detail: The diagnosis of acute appendicitis on CT typically involves identifying these combined findings.

questions.question: Gardner syndrome is a variant of Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP) that features colonic polyps plus:
choices: B. Osteomas and soft tissue tumors (desmoids)
C. Hyperpigmented macules on the lips
questions.detail: Gardner syndrome is specifically recognized for these extra-colonic manifestations alongside intestinal polyposis.

questions.question: Which polyposis syndrome is associated with thousands of polyps and an increased risk of CNS "gliomas"?
questions.detail: Turcot syndrome is characterized by the association of colonic polyposis with central nervous system tumors.

questions.question: "Epiploic appendagitis" is a benign mimic of diverticulitis characterized by a fat-density lesion with a:
questions.detail: The central dot represents a thrombosed central vein within the infarcted epiploic appendage.

questions.question: "Pylephlebitis" is a rare, serious complication of diverticulitis or appendicitis involving:
choices: B. Septic thrombophlebitis of the portal vein
questions.detail: In this condition, infection from the bowel spreads to the portal system and can lead to hepatic abscesses.

questions.question: The most common site for a colonic fistula in the setting of diverticulitis is the:
questions.detail: A colovesical fistula is a common complication that often presents clinically as pneumaturia, or air in the urine.
